html:
The COVID-19 pandemic reached India in January 2020 and hit hardest in the spring of 2021, when the Delta wave overwhelmed hospitals across the country.

In March 2020 the government ordered one of the strictest lockdowns in the world on four hours' notice. Millions of migrant workers, suddenly without work or transport, walked hundreds of kilometres home to their villages.

The first wave was milder than feared, and leaders spoke of victory. Then in April and May 2021 the Delta variant, first found in India, spread fast after state elections and religious gatherings. Hospitals ran out of beds and oxygen, families searched for cylinders on social media, and cremation grounds overflowed. Official deaths came to about 530,000, but the World Health Organization estimated about 4.7 million excess deaths by the end of 2021.

India also made vaccines for the world: the Serum Institute of India, the largest vaccine maker, produced the AstraZeneca shot, and India gave more than two billion doses at home.
sum: The COVID-19 pandemic reached India in January 2020 and hit hardest in the spring of 2021, when the Delta wave overwhelmed hospitals across the country.
